arcChoices.title: Norse Gods and Fate
arcChoices.description: Eight weeks on Odin, Thor, Loki, goddesses, fate, and Ragnarök.

topic.norse-edda-source.title: The Prose Edda as a source
topic.norse-edda-source.body: Snorri’s Prose Edda is a medieval handbook for poets. It preserves mythic stories, but it also organizes and explains them for a later Christian-era audience.

cards.title: A handbook, not a scripture
cards.body: The Prose Edda was written to help poets understand and compose traditional poetry. Its frame matters when we read it as evidence.

cards.title: Preservation with an agenda
cards.body: Snorri preserves older material while arranging it in a new literary and intellectual setting. That makes the work invaluable—and also not neutral.

topic.norse-wisdom-sacrifice.title: Wisdom and sacrifice
topic.norse-wisdom-sacrifice.body: Norse tradition repeatedly links knowledge to cost. Odin’s authority is not free power; it is knowledge gained through ordeal, exchange, and risk.

cards.title: Knowledge has a price
cards.body: Odin’s pursuit of wisdom is framed through sacrifice and bargaining. Intelligence and foresight are achieved, not merely possessed.

cards.title: A different heroic pressure
cards.body: Where Achilles asks what honor costs, Odin asks what foresight costs. That comparison works best when each tradition stays attached to its own sources.

topic.norse-genre-lens.title: Poetry, handbook, and myth
topic.norse-genre-lens.body: The Prose Edda teaches readers how poetic references work. That makes genre central: a mythic encyclopedia asks different questions from an epic or a play.

cards.title: Genre changes evidence
cards.body: A handbook can explain stories explicitly, but its organization is itself an interpretation. Track both the story and the frame.

cards.title: Use it carefully
cards.body: Snorri is essential for Norse mythology, but comparing him to Homer means comparing different kinds of work across different cultural moments.

topic.norse-power-cost.title: Power and cost
topic.norse-power-cost.body: Norse traditions repeatedly frame power through bargain, ordeal, and knowledge that exacts a price.

topic.norse-fate-end.title: Fate and the final ending
topic.norse-fate-end.body: Norse stories often build meaning from limits that cannot be escaped, including the approaching end of the gods.
